decisions.note: Round1 spec offered only a fallback title (no auto title/desc/favicon/preview) as an explicit scope option; client selected the metadata-fetching alternative.
Round1 spec had duplicates 'warn and keep existing'; client corrected to 'silently redirect to edit the existing bookmark' matching reference.
Round1 spec excluded import/export as an offered scope boundary; client selected including it.
Round1 spec had no notes field; client asked for a markdown notes area, never surfaced by maker.
Round1 spec's tag feature had no autocomplete; client requested tag-reuse suggestions.
Round1 stories omitted 'open bookmark navigates to url'; client called it 'the whole point'.
Round1 spec had no unread/read-later concept; client asked for it as a new pile.
Round1 spec had delete only, no reversible archive; client requested archive distinct from delete.
Round1 spec had no snapshot/preservation feature; client requested a saved copy of the page.
Round1 search was title/address keyword only; client asked for multi-field, case-insensitive, OR, and exact-phrase search.
Round1 spec had no sort capability; client requested sorting (newest/title).
Round1 spec had no bulk selection/action; client requested select-many bulk tag/archive/delete.
Round2 snapshot spec ('readable copy') had no PDF rule; client asked PDFs be kept as the raw file.
Round2 search spec only had OR/phrase; client asked for NOT-exclusion and parenthesised grouping.
Round2 search only supported click-to-filter tags; client asked for inline #tag typed in the search box.
Round2 bulk actions lacked mark-read/to-read, remove-tag, and select-all-matching; client requested all three.
Round2 spec had no saved-search/bundle concept; client asked to save a term+tag combo under a name.
Round2 spec had no persisted display prefs; client asked for remembered default sort order and larger text size (displayed-items count still missing, see miss).
Round2 list view didn't show tags per item; client asked to see tags in the list.
Snapshot feature (rounds 1-3) never included pushing to a public web-archive service; client raised it at the round3 gate (flagged as non-blocking).
